title: Shipped one game without AI, then tried it with Claude Code + Higgsfield. Two weeks later: a Steam page, a demo date and more fun (and hassle) than I expected.
author: noteasytobecheesy
selftext:
Hey, so I was getting intrigued by the multiple threads on X breaking down building games with AI and decided to give it a try. Had the idea and used only Claude Code (with the Unity MCP) for the project and Higgsfield for music, 3D turntables and the environment sounds. I was honestly just curious to see what’s possible now and how long it would take to push through the full Steam process, marketing included. 

First game took 2.5 years with a lot of back-and-forth and while I'm super proud of it, some parts are far from what I envisioned. For the 2nd game:

What worked:

Writing the idea as a plain design doc + [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) before any prompt. Everything else was easier because of it.

Tiny prompts with a clear “done”: one path tile, then guests walking, then a boat. One thing per session, playtest after each, commit after every working step.

Tests early. 290 now, including one that catches translated text overflowing buttons across all 14 languages - translations were AI too.

Letting it build tooling: when OBS lagged on my laptop, Claude built an in-engine replay recorder (frame-stepped capture, re-rendered audio). Every gameplay clip now comes from that.



What didn’t:

Debugging. Playtest, find bug, describe it, fix, repeat. The least fun part by a mile, and the messier my early prompts, the more of it I got.

Editor state drift: Unity settings changing under me after captures/builds. Solved with a rule that ProjectSettings gets restored from git after every tool run.

Result so far: Resortful, a cozy island resort sim, Steam page live, demo 2 Dec. Happy to share the [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) or prompt structure if anyone wants it. Curious what your first impressions are too :)

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5485070](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5485070)

replies.author: noteasytobecheesy
replies.body:
Trust me, there was a LOT of back-and-forth and some of the earlier assets looked like crap. For some reason, it kept cutting off edges and smudging them. So I devised a system after the 10th fail:

1. Generate 2D version of the design (dropped some reference images to give it guidance regarding style and look).  
2. Approve.  
3. Generate shots from every angle of the 2D design.  
4. Approve.  
5. Generate 3D version of the asset.  
6. Approve.  
7. Generate shots from every angle of the 3D design.  
8. Approve  
9. Animate

Got a bit tedious but cut down mistakes by 95%.
